proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the selected second-order law, the shrinking-margin phase diagram, a nominal-size counterexample, uniform local calibration, and a certified fixed-witness power gain; the D0.5 math referee passed them. The delivered package was graded subfield, below the fixed field floor, because its model scope and operational evidence remain narrow. A field-tier follow-on needs a broader design and usable calibration with finite-sample support.
tldr: Historical controls can raise the power of a distributional treatment test, but the Yang--Liu--Evans partial bootstrap enters a random-cutoff regime when historical and current controls differ by order \(N^{-1/2}\) and the equivalence margin shrinks at the same rate. The paper derives the exact selected quadratic-Gaussian rejection map, proves a nominal-size counterexample, and proves a current-control plug-in least-favorable calibration for the unchanged two-branch procedure. A replayable 256-bit MPFR/Arb outward-ball certificate now proves that this calibration retains a strict local-power gain at the fixed categorical witness.
